note: Phenotypic contamination via secondary DEE variants such as SCN8A is a plausible explanation for severe epilepsy discrepancies in early YWHAZ reports, though direct confirmation requires detailed cohort re-evaluation.

evidence.text: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies are severe, heterogeneous early-onset epilepsies with significant genetic complexity and overlapping phenotypic presentations.

source.title: Recent advances in epilepsy genomics and genetic testing
source.quote: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies (DEEs) are a group of severe, early onset epilepsies characterized by refractory seizures, developmental delay or regression associated with ongoing epileptic activity, and generally poor prognosis.

numbers.metric: Patients without a genetic diagnosis despite state-of-the-art testing
